memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "God listened to Leah, and she became pregnant and bore Jacob a fifth son. Then Leah said, 'God has rewarded me for giving my servant to my husband.' So she named him Issachar. Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son. Then Leah said, 'God has presented me with a precious gift. This time my husband will treat me with honor, because I have borne him six sons.' So she named him Zebulun. Some time later she gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah" - Gen 30:17-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Leah has more children, and her words begin to change in a hopeful direction. "God has rewarded me... God has presented me with a precious gift." At least she is looking upward, recognising that her children come from God's hand. Amid all the rivalry, there are flickers of faith in Leah — a woman learning, slowly, to see God at work in her life.

Yet the old ache still lingers. With Zebulun she says, "This time my husband will treat me with honor." Even after six sons, Leah is still hoping to finally win Jacob's love. Some wounds run deep and do not heal quickly. She keeps reaching for the affection that has always eluded her.

There is honesty and comfort here for us. Faith and unhealed longing often live side by side in the same heart. Leah could thank God for His gifts and still carry a deep, unsatisfied ache. That is the reality of many believers' lives — trusting God genuinely, yet still wrestling with old wounds.

If that is you, do not be discouraged. God is patient with our slow-healing hearts. He was gently drawing Leah, over years, to find her true satisfaction in Him rather than in her husband's approval. He is doing the same tender work in us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Are you learning to see God's hand and gifts in your daily life?
What old ache do you carry even alongside genuine faith?
Can you trust God's patient work in your slow-healing heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You are patient with my slow-healing heart. Help me to see Your good gifts, and draw me to find my deepest satisfaction in You alone. Amen.
